summary: The candidate correctly fixes the stale acc_linear_penalties reads and passes focused CPU and gfx950 tensor checks, but it does not advance the real min_new_tokens penalizer state in DFLASH/DSPARK decode preparation. Stop tokens can remain suppressed after the configured minimum, so this is a verified partial fix rather than a full contract fix.

tests.what_was_measured: Candidate regression against base: four failures and one pass; additive penalties were omitted and DSPARK incorrectly classified adjustments as a no-op.
Five focused candidate cases passed for additive-penalty broadcasting, dtype conversion, -inf masking, logit-bias composition, and the no-op predicate.
Ten existing DFlash logits tests passed.

On the assigned gfx950 GPU, two-row/four-position additive penalties plus logit bias exactly matched an explicit CPU reference, preserved -inf masks, and rejected invalid row count and zero draft-token inputs.
The real penalizer kept EOS at -inf without cumulate_output_tokens and lifted the mask only after two cumulations, while DFLASH decode preparation has no corresponding cumulation call.

gpu_evidence: AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950, single assigned GPU; affected tensor operation matched CPU reference exactly.
native_rebuild_reason: No native/C++ source changed in the candidate; Python modules were imported directly from the exact checkout.
remaining_counterexamples: With min_new_tokens=2, DFLASH/DSPARK decode preparation does not cumulate accepted output tokens, so the real EOS/stop-token adjustment can remain -inf after two or more generated tokens instead of being lifted at the minimum.
The candidate regression injects acc_additive_penalties directly and does not exercise creation, per-step advancement, refresh, or removal of the real min_new_tokens penalty.
The exact DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 HTTP serving reproduction remains unverified because only one gfx950 GPU and no qualified model weights were available.
remaining_limitations: No full-model DeepSeek-V4-Flash serving run, semantic generation validation, or TP4/distributed reproduction was possible.
The deterministic tiny Llama fixture cannot qualify the reported DSPARK model architecture and was not used as substitute proof.
GPU validation covers the affected tensor adjustment only, not the full serving engine path.
